Dec 2024 • Solo
I found this little gem of a restaurant by chance. Heat and fatigue from walking around the city led me to the nearest refuge. How lucky was that?

Very pleasantly surprised - and a nutella creme brulee to die for!
Sep 2019
We met with friends based locally at Ciao Bella during our one week visit of HCMC and throughly enjoyed our meal here.
We were welcomed with a glass of prosecco which was a nice touch and a very friendly and welcoming staff, including the owner/manager who came by several times to make sure that we were enjoying the food.
We skipped starters and 3 of us us chose the house special of 'posh carbonara' which was a little different to the usual but just delicious. the egg is poached and sits atop a whirl of pasta that has been mixed inside a half parmiggiano round to absorb the flavours and generous portion of it.Truffle oil was poured over the top, and it really was delicious.
One of our party chose the chicken parmiggiano over a bed of spaghetti in a wonderful, slightly sweet, tomato sauce. Fabulously crispy, just the right amount of cheese, and hugely generous portions on all fronts!
The desserts didn't disappoint either - a tiramisu, a chocolate lava cake, and a nutella creme brulee, which frankly should not be legal and as simply out of this world.

BIG TURN OFF AT THE END
Jun 2015 • Friends
Located on Dong Du Street, just a stone throw away from Sheraton Saigon Hotel, its location ensures that it's packed on most evenings. Luckily for us, we managed to secure a table without prior reservation.

Both my friend and I had the tomato soup. The soup was alright, but not really outstanding. Then we shared the Ciao Bella salad, which was good. The serving was much larger than we expected.

For main course, my friend had the Salmone Vignole and I had the Filleto di Manzo, rare. Both main course dishes were delicious and we enjoyed the meal, although we over ate.

It was a typical meal at a good restaurant, priced reasonably. The "high point" came at the end when we were settling the bill. We asked the waiter for a red official VAT invoice, but he replied that the restaurant does not provide that!

For the tourists and those who do not know, the official VAT invoice is the only invoice recognized by the Vietnamese tax authorities. It would be impossible for any business to do without it.

Frankly, I have no concern with how any establishment conduct its business. But if it is not prepared to issue customers with the official VAT invoice, then it should not be including VAT into the bill. 

For information, the crappy looking receipt you get when you pay your bill is not the VAT invoice. For any establishment to issue a VAT invoice, it needs to include the customer's name, address, and the tax code issued by the Vietnamese Tax Bureau.

What happened at Ciao Bella was a big turn off for me.

I am not Italian but I am well travelled and the food seems authentic to me- it is always reliable and you really need to book if you want to be sure of a table. Ciao Bella was a bit of fresh air compared to the hustle and bustle one might experience on a typical night in Saigon. The restaurant is located in the international district where you might find many foreigners (like myself) and expats. 

I must admit, I have never had Italian food in Saigon before so I have no real marker to compare the food against except for my experiences overseas, but that does not seem too fair since finding an Italian restaurant in this mostly non-diverse city is rare in itself. 

At any rate, I will say that the food was overall delicious and the ambience was a perfect setting for casual discussions or perhaps a night on the town with a date or a few intimate friends. I strongly suggest that you request a table upstairs for a few reasons. The downstairs tables are a bit tight and walking around is a bit uncomfortable. The bar area where the drinks were made for guests was a bit loud along with the distraction of guests coming and going. Besides the second floor being a bit quieter, the breeze above would make for a more relaxing evening, in my opinion. 

For the dinner entree, the table ordered risotto, spaghetti, the carbonara, and a salad with blue cheese (please excuse me for not remembering the correct menu names). Our guests (a few locals) enjoyed the spaghetti as I can imagine it is a dish that goes easy on anyone's palate. They also greatly enjoyed the risotto. As for myself, I had the carbonara which was mostly prepared right at our table. We really enjoyed that aspect. The salad with bleu cheese was fair, nothing spectacular. 

For dessert we ordered two dishes - the tiramisu and strawberry creme. Both were good, but our guests noted that the tiramisu was too sweet. The strawberry was perfect!

 Mostly, we were pleased that our guests had a comfortable and pleasant evening as Italian food was not part of their regular diet. We were happy to know they enjoyed their experience. We will definitely return to Ciao Bella!

I choose two things off the blackboard last night: the chargrilled octopus on a white bean, black olive and potato salad as a starter and the 'posh carbonara' as a main portion. The 'posh' refers to a large 'hollowed out' parmesan wheel brought to your table - like a giant bowl. The chef scrapes fresh cheese from around the inside of the wheel and adds some pepper. He also grinds fresh black pepper into the waiting serving bowl. Hot spaghetti arrives from the kitchen (having been cooked in garlic and cream) and is dropped into the parmesan wheel to be tossed with the freshly grated parmesan and pepper. It's then plated, on top of the black pepper in the bowl and topped with a couple of slices of proscuitto and a poached egg which is gently broken open so the yolk can run through the pile of spaghetti. A drizzle of truffle oil finishes the dish. Comp limoncello is served at the conclusion of the meal. Staff are efficient, friendly and knowledgable about the menu and wines. The chef was pleasant. If you get the chance to meet the owner, Tony, you're lucky. The pea ravioli with Parmesan and truffle oil I had in 2012, I vowed to order again this year, 2013, which is what I did just last night. This time, I invited the same colleague, and also my boss, to celebrate our last of 14 dinners in HCMC. Wow, how things have changed at Ciao Bella in just a year! Most noticeable was the serving size of the dish I had waited a year to have again. In 2012 a full order of pea ravioli was fit for a king with the taste and smell to go with it. This year, I could count the ravioli with one hand and maybe an extra digit from the other. I thought the waitress mistook what I said and put me down for a half order. My colleague and boss looked at my plate and chuckled; it was really small, especially for a big guy like me, 6'-4", 270lbs. Even the head waiter looked surprised, and had to double check with the staff to see if there wasn't a mix up. He came back and confirmed that what I got was in fact a full order. I didn't complain, and joked that the portion size was good for my health, thinking surely the smell and taste of the Parmesan cheese and truffle oil would more than make up for the lack of volume. But, sad to say, the flavor and smell just weren't there either. I am a truffle fanatic, and do not claim to be a food critic, but I do have a nose for truffles, and unless my olfactory sense was on holiday, I would bet my bottom Dong, there wasn't a gram of truffle oil in my dish! I'm even more confident that the Parmesan was not of the Parmigiano-Reggiano variety which would have brought the dish alive. But, in all fairness, the menu didn't state that it was Regianno. The head scratcher is that whatever they used in 2012 to make this dish so tasty, they must have left out this time. The Ciao Bella salad was nice, fresh, and enough to satisfy the 3 of us. The complimentary bread and 3 bread spreads (baked garlic, hummus, and flavored oil) were fine. My boss's squid ink spaghetti al nero di seppia (squid ink) with shrimp was generously sized, but ultimately did not live up to his expectation in terms of taste. My colleague said to mention that he enjoyed his lasagna. The best thing we had was the vino, a nice bottle of reasonably-priced red. The head waiter helped us make the right choice there, that's for sure. The rest of the staff was cordial but didn't warm our hearts like Tony did last year. Everything, with the exception of the wine was just so so. The bill, too, was not a stinger, so I'd say Ciao Bella fits the bill for someone on a semi tight budget on the hunt for carbohydrates and a decent bottle of wine. I come to HCMC every year, and last year Ciao Bella was the best Italian I had in HCMC, but this year the Italian place (Japanese-Italian fusion) that stole my heart was Pizza 4Ps -- want to try Italian with that wow factor? Try Pizza 4Ps. If nothing else, go for their magnificent, farm-fresh veggies and cheeses, stay for their 3 to 5 cheese pizzas, or out-of-this-world marinara spaghetti.

Finally got the carbonara I'd been craving!
Feb 2013
Ciao Bella is a lovely little Italian restaurant conveniently located in Ho Chi Minh City (around 5 minutes in a taxi from our hostel in District 1). We ate an early lunch there, and were pleased to be in time to choose the 'three course set' menu, which was delicious if a little pricey compared to your standard Vietnamese cuisine. The three courses set us back around 190.000vnd each (around $10usd), so it was by no means expensive compared to western standards.

We were given the opportunity to choose between soup (carrot or potato) or salad (mixed or Caesar) as a starter. I went for the Caesar salad, and it was really tasty. A lot of the greenery in Vietnamese cuisine is made up of mint, basil and other herbs - which made real lettuce a nice change. Ben chose the potato soup, which was also very nice and served hot.

For main, we had the choice of around ten different dishes including pasta choices and also other meals such as chicken breast with sides. I chose spaghetti carbonara, and Ben had the linguine with clams. I was so relieved to taste a real carbonara sauce - I'd ordered the same dish elsewhere the night before and it wasn't nearly as tasty. Both mains were great.

The set menu also included dessert and coffee. I ordered a latte and Ben a cappuccino, which were both lovely if a little hot compared to western standards. We were each served a slice of banana bread for dessert, which had nice flavours but was quite dry. 

Staff were very attentive without being overbearing, they were diligent in refilling our water glasses as required. I can strongly recommend Ciao Bella as a Saigon eatery, and can testify that the three course set lunch menu is great value (and delicious!).

After having tried Pizza 4Ps, I was doubtful if any other Italian place would come even close. Well, Ciao Bella does come pretty close.
